authorities.locator: Section 1291, preliminary edition current through July 29, 2026
authorities.proposition: The courts of appeals have jurisdiction over appeals from final decisions of the district courts, subject to statutory exceptions not implicated by the final amended judgment in this synthetic diversity action.

A pre-verdict JMOL motion must specify the judgment sought and supporting law and facts; a timely postverdict motion renews that motion and may join a Rule 59 request. If renewed JMOL is granted, the court must conditionally rule on the new-trial motion, and if JMOL is reversed the conditional new trial proceeds unless the appellate court orders otherwise.

After a jury trial, a federal court may grant a new trial on all or some issues for recognized federal grounds. A party's motion is due within 28 days after judgment; if the court acts on its own initiative it must give notice and specify its reasons.

authorities.locator: Rule 4(a)(1)(A) and Rule 4(a)(4)(A)(i), (v) in the official appellate rules
authorities.proposition: In a civil case with no United States party, notice ordinarily is due 30 days after judgment. A timely Rule 50(b) motion or Rule 59 new-trial motion causes the appeal period to run from the order disposing of the last such remaining motion.

authorities.citation: Unitherm Food Systems, Inc. v. Swift-Eckrich, Inc., 546 U.S. 394 (2006)
authorities.proposition: Rule 50 establishes related pre-verdict and postverdict stages. A proper renewed motion is essential to appellate sufficiency relief because it lets the trial judge first evaluate the verdict and possible new-trial consequences; a party cannot obtain appellate merits relief on a subject that was not properly renewed after verdict.

authorities.citation: Price v. City of Charlotte, 93 F.3d 1241 (4th Cir. 1996)
authorities.proposition: The reason offered for judgment as a matter of law must be raised in the Rule 50(a) motion and reasserted under Rule 50(b), thereby apprising the court and opposing party of the asserted insufficiency while correction before jury submission remains possible.

authorities.locator: Nos. 24-1445 and 24-1488, official slip opinion pages 10–11
authorities.proposition: A distinct physical-proximity basis first raised in Rule 50(b) was unavailable even though the general sufficiency issue raised in Rule 50(a) remained reviewable.

authorities.citation: Wiener v. AXA Equitable Life Insurance Co., 153 F.4th 413 (4th Cir. 2025)
authorities.proposition: Variation between the Rule 50(b) issue and appellate theory need not align perfectly when the same issue was raised; it does not establish Rule 50(a)-to-Rule 50(b) preservation.

authorities.citation: Boley v. Armor Correctional Health Services, Inc., No. 23-1493 (4th Cir. Dec. 30, 2024) (unpublished)
authorities.proposition: The unpublished majority explained that Rule 50(b) is limited to grounds advanced under Rule 50(a), serving notice, cure, fairness, and Seventh Amendment interests. Its separate discussion of fundamental-error review is nonprecedential and is not used as the controlling rule for Blue Ember.

authorities.citation: Boley v. Armor Correctional Health Services, Inc., No. 23-1493 (4th Cir. Dec. 30, 2024) (Quattlebaum, J., concurring)
authorities.locator: Concurrence, official slip opinion pages 29 and 36-41
authorities.proposition: The unpublished concurrence read Unitherm to foreclose appellate review of a Rule 50 issue that was not properly presented through both stages. It documents the remedial tension but supplies no binding circuit rule.

authorities.citation: Atlas Food Systems & Services, Inc. v. Crane National Vendors, Inc., 99 F.3d 587 (4th Cir. 1996)
authorities.locator: Nos. 95-1717 and 95-1718, official slip opinion pages 7-9 and 17-18
authorities.proposition: A district court may grant a Rule 59 new trial when the verdict is against the clear weight of the evidence, rests on false evidence, or would cause a miscarriage of justice; appellate review is for abuse of discretion. A partial retrial is proper only when the retained and retried issues are distinct and separable without injustice or jury confusion.

authorities.citation: Rice v. Community Health Association, 203 F.3d 283 (4th Cir. 2000)
authorities.proposition: A new trial may be limited to a distinct and separable damages issue when no injustice will result, preserving settled issues while serving economy, fairness, and repose.

authorities.citation: Thermal Design, Inc. v. M&M Builders, Inc., 207 N.C. App. 79, 698 S.E.2d 516 (2010)
authorities.locator: Official North Carolina Appellate Reports pages 88-90, 698 S.E.2d at 523-24
authorities.proposition: A party injured by breach must use due care to minimize loss, while the breaching party bears the burden to prove a failure to mitigate and the amount by which recoverable damages should be reduced.

authorities.citation: Clark v. Bichsel, 239 N.C. App. 13, 767 S.E.2d 145 (2015)
authorities.locator: Official North Carolina Appellate Reports page 17, 767 S.E.2d at 148
authorities.proposition: Failure to mitigate damages is an affirmative defense, placing the issue on the party asserting the reduction rather than shifting the ultimate contract-damages burden to the injured party.
